title: From Numbers to Names, a facial-recognition search, finds two Holocaust survivors in archive photographs
summary: The From Numbers to Names face search found Geddy Lee's mother in a photograph from the Bergen-Belsen displaced-persons camp, and survivor Blanche Fixler recognized herself in photos that it found.
account: From Numbers to Names (N2N) is a facial-recognition search built by the software engineer Daniel Patt. It indexes roughly half a million digitized Holocaust-era photographs from the US Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM) and Yad Vashem. In an interview that The Times of Israel published on 26 June 2022, Patt said that the tool had surfaced a photograph of Mary Weinrib at the Bergen-Belsen displaced-persons camp. She was an Auschwitz survivor and the mother of the Rush musician Geddy Lee. The interview does not give the date of the identification. According to Patt, Lee confirmed the identification and then located further photographs of his mother's extended family in the Yad Vashem collection. On 28 June 2022 The Jerusalem Post published a Jewish Telegraphic Agency story that draws on the interview and adds that Mary Weinrib died in summer 2021. BBC News reported on 12 November 2022 that the tool found the survivor Blanche Fixler in a wartime group photo held by the US Holocaust Memorial Museum, which had listed her as unidentified. Her recognition raised the number of identified people in the photo from three to six. Scott Miller, the museum's director of curatorial affairs, told the BBC that such identifications restore "some semblance of dignity" to the people pictured. On 19 December 2022 NPR reported that Patt had searched using a photo from Twitter, and that Fixler recognized herself, her aunt and her cousin in the photographs that the tool found.
purpose: From Numbers to Names was built to help identify unnamed faces in Holocaust-era photo and video archives and to help descendants find images of relatives. Both identifications are that intended benefit.
system: From Numbers to Names (N2N) facial-recognition search
developer: Daniel Patt (independent project; N2N volunteer team)

ratings.reason: Patt reports that Lee confirmed a photograph of his mother at Bergen-Belsen and then found photographs of her extended family. Fixler found images of herself, her aunt and her cousin (NPR, BBC).

The BBC reports that Fixler's recognition doubled the number of identified people in one US Holocaust Memorial Museum photo, from three to six. No source records a formal archive update for the Lee photograph.
Two documented identifications among the millions of unidentified faces that the tool indexes are a small benefit to society.

fields.summary: The From Numbers to Names face search found Geddy Lee's mother in a photograph from the Bergen-Belsen displaced-persons camp, and survivor Blanche Fixler recognized herself in photos that it found.
fields.account: From Numbers to Names (N2N) is a facial-recognition search built by the software engineer Daniel Patt. It indexes roughly half a million digitized Holocaust-era photographs from the US Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM) and Yad Vashem. In an interview that The Times of Israel published on 26 June 2022, Patt said that the tool had surfaced a photograph of Mary Weinrib at the Bergen-Belsen displaced-persons camp. She was an Auschwitz survivor and the mother of the Rush musician Geddy Lee. The interview does not give the date of the identification. According to Patt, Lee confirmed the identification and then located further photographs of his mother's extended family in the Yad Vashem collection. On 28 June 2022 The Jerusalem Post published a Jewish Telegraphic Agency story that draws on the interview and adds that Mary Weinrib died in summer 2021. BBC News reported on 12 November 2022 that the tool found the survivor Blanche Fixler in a wartime group photo held by the US Holocaust Memorial Museum, which had listed her as unidentified. Her recognition raised the number of identified people in the photo from three to six. Scott Miller, the museum's director of curatorial affairs, told the BBC that such identifications restore "some semblance of dignity" to the people pictured. On 19 December 2022 NPR reported that Patt had searched using a photo from Twitter, and that Fixler recognized herself, her aunt and her cousin in the photographs that the tool found.
